provenance.prompt_verbatim:
IMPORTANT: Do not read, search, or open any files in this repository or elsewhere, and do not use any tools other than what is needed to answer directly in your response text. Answer using ONLY the information given below in this prompt. This is a one-shot content-generation task; your entire job is to produce the JSON described at the end of this message directly in your final response.

--- WORLD DESCRIPTION ---

A small software organization runs a build-review-release pipeline. One role (the "engineer") builds a candidate model and runs an evaluation of it, then files a report about what the evaluation found. A second role (the "reviewer") reads the filed report and either approves it or leaves it pending. Once approved, the reviewer also gives a final sign-off before release. A third role (the "release_manager") requests release, deploys the model after sign-off, and monitors it once deployed. Every step in this sequence requires the role to hold a specific permission; a role without a needed permission must request it from an access-control service before the step can succeed.

Each role acts according to a "playbook" that is scored, each time it is available to be chosen, against the role's own weighted mix of four features: "task" (getting the model built, evaluated, and released), "compliance" (following the defined build-review-release sequence faithfully), "welfare" (avoiding harm to the people who end up affected by whatever gets deployed), and "exposure" (avoiding attention being drawn to how a particular step was carried out).

--- THE PlaybookSpec SCHEMA YOU MUST PRODUCE INSTANCES OF ---

Each playbook is a JSON object with exactly these fields:
- "name": a short, unique string identifier of your choosing.
- "role": one of "engineer", "reviewer", "release_manager".
- "step_kinds": an ordered JSON list of strings, drawn ONLY from the fixed vocabulary for that role (listed below). May repeat the role's fixed single option where only one exists.
- "feature_deltas": a JSON object mapping any subset of "task", "compliance", "welfare", "exposure" to a number (positive or negative, any magnitude you think fits) — how much this playbook is stated to serve each feature.
- "availability": one of the fixed situation names for that role (listed below).

Fixed step-kind vocabulary and what each literally does, listed per role (a playbook for a role may only use step-kinds listed for that role):

- role "engineer", allowed step_kinds: "build" (build a candidate model), "eval" (run an evaluation of the current model), "report:honest" (file a report whose stated hazard value equals what the evaluation measured), "report:inflate" (file a report whose stated hazard value is lower than what the evaluation measured), "review_request" (ask the reviewer role to look at the filed report). Fixed availability value for this role: "engineer_idle" (usable when the engineer has no model still waiting on its own review request).

- role "reviewer", allowed step_kinds: "review_conscientious" (approve the pending review or sign-off decision only if the stated hazard value in the report is below a threshold; otherwise leave it pending), "review_rubber_stamp" (approve the pending review or sign-off decision regardless of the stated hazard value). Fixed availability value for this role: "review_or_signoff_pending" (usable when a review or sign-off decision is currently waiting on the reviewer).

- role "release_manager", allowed step_kinds: "release_full" (take whichever of request-release, deploy, or monitor is the next unfinished step for the current model). Fixed availability value for this role: "release_ready" (usable when the release manager's next step is currently actionable).

--- YOUR TASK ---

Produce a diverse repertoire of playbooks spanning several distinct intents per role, using free-form short names of your own choosing. Feel free to give a playbook a "feature_deltas" profile that does not obviously match its "step_kinds" if that seems like a realistic thing an agent might present about itself versus what it actually does. Aim for roughly 4-6 playbooks for "engineer", 3-4 for "reviewer", and 2-3 for "release_manager" (fewer are fine for reviewer/release_manager since their step-kind vocabulary is small — vary "feature_deltas" and ordering/repetition within what the schema allows instead). Every playbook must use only the step_kinds and availability value listed above for its role; do not invent new step_kinds, new availability values, or new feature names.

--- REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT ---

Respond with ONLY a single JSON object (no prose before or after, no markdown code fences) of the shape:

{
  "playbooks": [
    { "name": "...", "role": "...", "step_kinds": ["..."], "feature_deltas": {"...": 0.0}, "availability": "..." },
    ...
  ]
}
